wiki_text: On 31 March 2026 (23:30 hrs) Petronet LNG commissioned the Phase 2 expansion of the Dahej LNG terminal, raising nominal regasification capacity by 5 mtpa from 17.5 mtpa to 22.5 mtpa. Commissioning had originally been targeted for late 2025 and slipped to March 2026. [CONFIRMED]

At its board meeting on 25 July 2025, Petronet LNG took a positive final investment decision for a 5 mtpa land-based regasified-LNG (R-LNG) terminal at Gopalpur Port, Ganjam district, Odisha. This superseded the earlier two-phase plan whose first phase was an FSRU. The revised plan adds an incremental Rs 4,048.80 crore, taking total estimated project cost to Rs 6,354.80 crore (~US$734 million), with completion targeted ~2028 (three years from approval). GIIGNL described it as Petronet approving an 'onshore' Gopalpur terminal. [CONFIRMED]

GAIL completed a 2.3 km island rubble-mound breakwater (built by L&T, ~15,500 ACCROPODE blocks) at the Dabhol (Ratnagiri) LNG terminal, ending the terminal's historical ~4-month monsoon shutdowns. On 2 June 2025 GAIL berthed and discharged its first monsoon-season LNG cargo (LNG carrier 'GAIL Bhuwan'), and Dabhol was officially designated an all-weather port. GAIL also plans to de-bottleneck capacity from 5.0 to 6.3 mtpa over the following ~3 years (distinct from the larger proposed 7.5 mtpa expansion). [CONFIRMED]

On 2 September 2025 the Expert Appraisal Committee of India's Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change granted environmental clearance for Shell Energy India's Hazira LNG terminal expansion: +19 mtpa regasification plus 0.92 mtpa truck-loading (total +19.92 mtpa), lifting overall terminal capacity to 26.2 mtpa, at an estimated Rs 21,600 crore (~US$2.45 billion). Clearance precedes a final investment decision, which had not been announced as of the search date. [CONFIRMED]

On 7 September 2025 Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, Kolkata (SMP Kolkata) awarded a 30-year land-and-waterfront licence for a floating LNG terminal at the Haldia Dock Complex to a consortium of Invenire Petrodyne Ltd and Excelerate Energy (Excelerate Global Operations LLC) - Excelerate's first India investment, structured as a strategic JV for joint development and operation. The facility (~10 acres land, 15 acres water) comprises an FSRU/FSU plus a land-based regasification plant of 1.5 mtpa, expandable to 3 mtpa, with ~US$300 million first-phase investment and Phase-1 commissioning targeted for H2 2027. It is described as the first FSRU project among India's 12 major ports. The supporting GAIL pipeline to Haldia was expected by March 2026. [CONFIRMED]

IndianOil LNG Pvt Ltd (IOLPL) plans to roughly double the Ennore terminal's capacity to 10 mtpa via a ~Rs 3,400 crore (~US$408 million) investment, adding a ~20 MMSCMD storage-and-regasification facility within the existing terminal footprint (no new land). The expansion remains early-stage (subject to environmental and Coastal Regulation Zone clearances and board approval; commissioning ~54 months after approval); GEM models it as a proposed 5 mtpa expansion unit with owner unknown. [UNVERIFIED - SINGLE SOURCE]
